answer: Each epoch a beacon lights a perch on the horizon, and a falcon — a stranger-auditor chosen by lot — flies out to inspect it. A perch is earned only by a receipt for a real job done since the last flash, so a fresh clone starts with an empty perch. Perches funded from one trail sit on one horizon line, and the falcon sees them as a single roost: it lands once and drops one fish. The toll to summon the falcon squares with the perches on a line, so n clones pay n perches and n squared in toll yet split one fish, while one honest agent builds one perch and keeps the whole catch.
